title: The Internet In Eight Round Trips

vo.text: Eight hidden trips across the internet — that's what hitting enter does.
Your browser doesn't know where that is.
It asks a resolver, which asks a root server, then a dot-com server, then the site's own server, for the real address.
But before any of that page arrives, the two computers shake hands three times just to connect.
Then five more times to lock it with encryption. Eight round trips, and the request still hasn't been sent.
Finally, the server sends back the page's code. Your browser builds it and paints every pixel — sixty times a second.
All of that, before you've finished blinking.

beats.visual: frame-0 composed: finished browser window loaded with dailybyte.com (header, hero image block, article lines); a faint already-complete route ribbon (laptop -> DNS node -> server rack) glows beneath it; stat chip '8 ROUND TRIPS'

camera pulls back from the browser into a node diagram: laptop (typed address) -> resolver node -> root-server node (chip '13 ROOT SERVER GROUPS WORLDWIDE') -> .com TLD-server node -> authoritative-server node (rack icon); packet dot travels the chain, 'IP found' label flies back to the laptop
zoom to laptop <-> server rack; packet bounces 3x (SYN / SYN-ACK / ACK, counter 1-3), padlock assembles over 5 more bounces (counter 4-8); '8' stamp lands, kicker 'REQUEST NOT EVEN SENT YET'

server rack fires back an HTML-document-shaped packet; browser window re-forms around it; small DOM-tree nodes assemble inside the page outline, then a paint-color sweep washes left to right; readout '60 FPS - 16.67 ms/frame'
diagram overlays dissolve away, landing exactly on the hook's finished browser window (last frame == frame 0); no CTA
